articles.title_orig: America’s most expensive neighborhood with $500M homes on verge of collapse: ‘Ego got in the way’
articles.title_zh: America’s most expensive neighborhood with $500M homes on verge of collapse: ‘Ego got in the way’
articles.content_orig:
A Malibu hilltop enclave, once billed as the most expensive new neighborhood in America, is on the verge of collapse.
Four of its five mansions are unsold, and the developer is locked in a bitter bankruptcy fight with his financial partner.
The project, known as the Case, is the work of developer Scott Gillen.
Gillen paid $50 million in 2017 for a 24-acre ocean-view parcel — then a record for undeveloped land in Malibu, The Wall Street Journal reported.
He planned five sleek homes inspired by California’s midcentury Case Study Houses, priced from about $40 million to $100 million each. Together, he hoped they would sell for close to half a billion dollars.
Nearly a decade later, only one home has sold, for $61 million in 2024, according to property records cited by the Journal. The other four are nearly complete but still on the market.
Real estate agents who worked on the project said the developer was largely to blame.
“Ego just got in the way,” Compass agent Tracy Tutor, who worked on sales at the Case in 2019, told the New York-based paper.
This summer, entities tied to Gillen filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection.
The filings list a long roster of creditors, from landscapers and a security firm to subcontractors. They also show outstanding loans from JPMorgan Chase and an entity tied to the bridge lender Private Mortgage Fund.
The largest debt is owed to a company tied to Los Angeles developer and investor Barry Shy, Gillen’s partner. Shy’s company says it provided a $260 million promissory note to the project in 2021. Shy claims Gillen now owes him more than $240 million with interest. Gillen disputes that, saying in court documents that the outstanding principal is $89 million.
Shy has accused Gillen of mismanaging the project and wants a court-appointed receiver to take control. Gillen, in turn, has accused Shy of fraud and self-dealing. He says Shy cut off funding in 2025 to squeeze him out. Gillen also claims Shy threatened to block a $110 million sale of two of the homes to an affiliate of billionaire Don Hankey.
Agents described Gillen as a perfectionist who insisted on attending showings and pitching buyers himself, which often put them off. Tutor said that at one promotional party, guests were asked to remove their shoes and the toilets were covered in plastic wrap so no one could use them.
Agents also said ultra-wealthy buyers balked at paying tens of millions of dollars for a home next door to a nearly identical one.
Josh Altman, a former “Million Dollar Listing Los Angeles” star, said the prices were unrealistic from the start. “He could have sold [the houses] 10 times over at a reasonable price,” Altman said.
Gillen refused to budge. “We’re not going to adjust our prices,” he told the Journal in 2023.
The broader Malibu market has also softened since the Palisades fire in early 2025.
As of mid-October, 160 Malibu homes had been cut below their original asking prices, with a median reduction of 8.9%, according to the website Luxury Price Drops.
The Journal also reported a previously unreported 1987 murder charge against Gillen, who then went by Scott Ashley. He was ultimately convicted of the lesser offense of accessory to a felony and placed on felony probation.
In an Instagram post last month, he vowed never to give up and said the project was almost finished.
“Whatever you do, you fight the fight never stop and you never give up,” he wrote. “I remember when I bought this dirt, lizards, and snakes that’s what I got. Look at it now, I get to look say yeah I did that s—. We’re almost there just a little bit more. Have a fantastic day.”

articles.title_orig: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
articles.title_zh: NASA is looking for astronauts to live and work on the Moon
articles.content_orig:
The NASA logo is seen at NASA's Johnson Space Center, Friday, Aug. 28, 2026, in Houston. Karen Warren/AP hide caption
If you have dreams of going to the moon, you now have a chance. NASA is accepting applications for those interested in becoming an astronaut.
The candidates selected to be astronauts would not only test spacecraft but would also live and work on the moon in a future moon base, said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman in a statement released on Saturday.
"Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage," the statement said. "NASA's astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation."
There are currently 32 active astronauts in NASA's astronaut corps. Since NASA missions began in the 1960s, the agency has selected 370 people to train as astronauts, according to the agency.
The applicant process is extremely competitive. Out of more than 8,000 applicants for NASA's last astronaut class, only 10 candidates were selected.
While any U.S. citizen can apply and there is no official age restriction, applicants will need to have a master's degree in a STEM-related field such as engineering or math.
In a recent change, a nursing degree qualifies.
"Nursing degrees are now included in the STEM definition," Anna Schneider, NASA spokesperson, told NPR on Sunday. "Master's-level nursing degrees now meet the minimum educational requirement, whereas nursing degrees were previously excluded."
In addition, NASA is requiring a minimum of three years of related professional experience after completing a degree.
In lieu of a master's degree and working experience, NASA will consider those in a PhD program (in STEM), doctors or pilots with extensive flight experience.
FILE - This detail of a July 20, 1969 photo made available by NASA shows astronaut Neil Armstrong reflected in the helmet visor of Buzz Aldrin on the surface of the moon. Neil Armstrong/NASA via AP hide caption
If chosen, the selected astronauts will undergo training that will last for two years. NASA said astronauts will prepare for critical and difficult missions such as landing near the moon's South Pole.
To achieve its goal of returning humans to the moon in 2028 – the first time since 1972 – NASA is relying on private companies such as Blue Origin and SpaceX to develop systems and spacecraft.
During a Nov. 7 press conference on the Artemis III moon mission's progress, Isaacman said he is "very confident" the mission will launch in 2027.
The starting salary is $164,395 and applications will be received through Dec. 3.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone who makes such an offer or request is not an NPR employee and does not represent NPR.

articles.title_orig: When the Boss on the Phone Isn’t Real: How More Than $129 Million Was Stolen Using A.I.
articles.title_zh: When the Boss on the Phone Isn’t Real: How More Than $129 Million Was Stolen Using A.I.
articles.content_orig:
Two Israeli men were among three individuals charged for their alleged involvement in a fraud scheme that used artificial intelligence to impersonate CEOs and steal over $129 million from companies around the world, according to documents unsealed by the FBI and the US Attorney's Office (USAO) for the Southern District of New York on Thursday.
Israeli national Sharon Hazan and dual Israeli-Emirati national Guy Sheetrit, along with co-conspirator and dual Spanish-British national Jacob Soall, were all charged with multiple counts of crimes related to wire fraud, money laundering, and identity theft in relation to the scheme.
According to the USAO, the three men are accused of beginning each instance of the fraud scheme by choosing employees at companies to target.
They allegedly used AI to falsify the voice and image of each company's CEO and communicated with targeted employees, claiming they needed them to carry out a large, secret financial transaction.
The USAO claimed that while presenting themselves as the CEO, co-conspirators instructed the employee to contact lawyers at large international law firms they said were working on the transaction. To convince the employee that the fraudulent financial transfer was legitimate, they also impersonated the lawyers.
A co-conspirator impersonating a lawyer then allegedly directed the employee to wire a large amount of money to bank accounts controlled by additional, unidentified co-conspirators in other countries, such as Spain, Portugal, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Austria, Slovakia, and China.
Once the affected companies' employees wired the money, the co-conspirators are accused of converting it into cryptocurrency to conceal the origin and ownership of the stolen funds before distributing it amongst themselves.
Through the scheme, they allegedly stole over $129 million from various companies across the US and the world, including $11,578,474 from a UK-based financial technology company, $4,829,580 from a hospital system headquartered in Missouri, $5,242,747 from a Florida-based pet food company, and $2,968,497 from another hospital system headquartered in California.
Soall is accused of primarily impersonating the fake lawyers used in the scheme, using a script to sound like a real attorney when speaking with targeted employees and convincing them not to discuss the financial transaction with other employees. He was arrested in Spain on July 17.
Hazan was accused of being responsible for much of the money laundering in the scam, along with other involvement. He allegedly bragged that he had laundered over $400 million in the past few years and claimed to be “number one all over the world” among professional money launderers.
Hazan was previously convicted of fraud charges in New York in 2008 and was arrested for the AI scam in Spain on September 7.
Sheetrit was also allegedly involved in the fraud scheme’s money laundering efforts and other activities before being arrested in the United Kingdom on September 7.
Extradition requests for the three co-conspirators are pending. If charged, they face maximum sentences of 20 years per count for conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, money laundering conspiracy, and two counts of money laundering, plus two years per count for two counts of aggravated identity theft.

articles.title_orig: "Forever cruise" arrested at Singapore port, court records show
articles.title_zh: "Forever cruise" arrested at Singapore port, court records show
articles.content_orig:
The Odyssey, the "forever cruise" that has been stranded in Southeast Asia after its owner struggled with financial problems , has been arrested in Singapore, according to court records obtained by CBS News.
A Singaporean law firm, Helmsman LLC, is listed as the arresting solicitor, but it is unclear whom the firm is representing. A source familiar with the matter tells CBS News that it is likely a fuel supplier.
The luxury cruise ship is currently being operated by its lender after its owner, Villa Vie Residences, couldn't keep up with payments.
Villa Vie owes one supplier in the area approximately $500,000, though it's unclear whether that supplier hired the law firm to solicit the arrest.
A ship arrest is a legal process in which a vessel can be detained or seized following a legal claim.
The journey of the MV Odyssey luxury cruise ship, launched in October 2024, came to a sudden end last month in Cambodia, where residents on the ship had just hours to disembark.
According to accounts from multiple sources familiar with the final weeks on board, these details included a scramble to find fuel while stuck at a port in Singapore, a rush by the crew to obtain provisions once food shipments had ended, and the temporary detainment of the ship in Hong Kong.
This story published first on CBS News at 6:24 p.m. on Nov. 8, 2026.

articles.title_orig: Targeted by U.S., Armed Group Strikes Back in Colombia
articles.title_zh: Targeted by U.S., Armed Group Strikes Back in Colombia
articles.content_orig:
A drone attack on a military base in northern Colombia has killed three soldiers and wounded at least 16, the country’s armed forces said.
The Colombian military said in a statement on Saturday that the attack hit a base in Santa Rosa del Sur, a small town in the foothills of the San Lucas mountain range. Authorities have not said who carried out the strike, the latest in a series of attacks on security forces as violence rises across rural parts of the country.
The area is rich in gold mines and has long been disputed by rebel armed groups including the Gulf Clan, the National Liberation Army (ELN) and smaller groups led by former members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC).
Footage shared on social media showed clouds of smoke rising from the base after three explosions, and soldiers taking cover in shelters made of sandbags.
“Those who were behind this attack… will have nowhere to hide,” President Abelardo de la Espriella wrote on X. “Every attack against our soldiers strengthens our resolve to defend Colombia.”
Violence has intensified in several rural areas since de la Espriella, a conservative, took office in August.
The president cancelled peace talks with rebel groups and has taken a confrontational approach, including more air strikes, deploying more troops in some cities and creating joint task forces to defend strategic assets such as a pipeline that runs from the Caribbean coast to central Colombia.
De la Espriella’s government argues that armed groups used ceasefires granted by the previous government to consolidate their grip on rural areas, where they tax local businesses and profit from the drug trade.
Some groups have responded by stepping up attacks on the country’s armed forces.
Last week, a military base in Tolima province was targeted with missiles made from gas canisters. The attack killed four civilians, including a two-month-old baby.
Police in the border city of Cucuta have been attacked several times with remotely activated bombs.
State forces and illegal armed groups carried out 34 attacks with bombs or explosives in Colombia in the four weeks to October 16, a 9 percent increase on last year’s four-week average, according to ACLED, a group that monitors armed conflicts.
A 2016 peace deal with FARC led to the demobilisation of more than 14,000 fighters, but smaller groups have since fought over the rebels’ former territory.

articles.title_orig: Iran vows ‘astonishing’ strikes and lifts missile-range limit as US targets land routes
articles.title_zh: Iran vows ‘astonishing’ strikes and lifts missile-range limit as US targets land routes
articles.content_orig:
Iran proxy attacks target a key Saudi Arabian oil pipeline as host Kayleigh McEnany reports on the expanding conflict. Former Navy SEAL Jack Carr joins the program to discuss ballistic missile production and Chinese satellite intelligence linked to a strike killing three American troops. Carr warns that Houthis threaten global shipping chokepoints near the Red Sea.
Iran lifted its self-imposed ballistic missile-range limit and threatened to unleash new, homegrown weapons that would "astonish the entire world," within hours of the U.S. military launching a new task force aimed at choking off Tehran's weapons shipments and illicit trade Nov. 7.
Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) spokesperson Brig. Gen. Hossein Mohebbi confirmed that Iran was now abandoning its previous 2,000-kilometer, or roughly 1,240-mile, ballistic missile-range restriction, according to The Associated Press .
"That restriction has been lifted for us," Mohebbi clarified in the wake of the task force announcement.
RUSSIA SECRETLY BOLSTERED IRAN'S MISSILE ARSENAL BEFORE WAR WITH US, RECORDS UNCOVER
FILE PHOTO: Iranian missiles are displayed at the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Aerospace Force Museum in Tehran, Iran, November 15, 2024. Majid Asgaripour/WANA (West Asia press Agency) via REUTERS
U.S. Central Command established "Task Force Iron Gate", an initiative targeting the movement of advanced Iranian weapons systems, dual-use materials and illicit revenue across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea.
"Strengthening CENTCOM's collaboration with US Interagency partners will further constrain Iran's ability to finance terrorism, rebuild weapons factories, and replenish their military," Adm. Brad Cooper, commander of U.S. Central Command, said in a statement shared on X.
According to Behnam Taleblu, senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies ( FDD ), the U.S. may now carry out "targeted strikes" against facilitators while putting "political pressure on bordering states, as well as market and sanctions pressure against institutions underwriting Iran’s illicit trade."
"It speaks volumes, of course, that this effort is being stood up within CENTCOM headquarters," Taleblu told Fox News Digital.
Meanwhile, Iran's IRGC quickly dismissed the new initiative as "wordplay," claiming Tehran had already made preparations and coordinated with neighboring countries to withstand additional pressure, Fars News Agency reported.
Mohebbi also warned that Iran was developing new weapons capable of delivering devastating blows in another confrontation with the U.S. and Israel .
IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS
An Iranian missile is launched during a military exercise in an undisclosed location in Iran, August 20, 2025. (Iranian Army/WANA (West Asia News Agency)/Handout via REUTERS)
"There are surprises that will be unveiled and deployed on the battlefield if a third wave of confrontation with the enemy erupts. These surprises will astonish the entire world," Mohebbi said during a news conference in Tehran on Saturday, according to Iran's state-run Islamic Republic News Agency ( IRNA ).
"If they once again miscalculate, or if the Zionists, in pursuit of their own interests, lead the criminal United States into another miscalculation, they should know that Iran's next blows will be even harder and will leave them crippled for years to come," he added.
Iran's previous 2,000-kilometer limit already placed the entire Arabian Peninsula, the Levant, most of Egypt and parts of Greece and the Balkans within range.
In March, Iran unsuccessfully attempted to strike the joint U.S.-British military base on Diego Garcia in the Indian Ocean, roughly 2,500 miles from the Islamic Republic.
Mohebbi also claimed Iran was preparing to unveil new underground missile facilities, as Tehran seeks to shield its weapons production from future attacks.
The installations, described by Iranian officials as "missile cities," are designed to allow the IRGC to continue manufacturing weapons during wartime, according to IRNA.
TRUMP'S MOAB THREAT COULD PUT IRAN'S DEEPEST BUNKERS IN AMERICA'S CROSSHAIRS
Diego Garcia, the largest island in the Chagos archipelago and site of a major United States military base in the middle of the Indian Ocean leased from the U.K. in 1966. (reuters)
The IRGC spokesman claimed Iran's Aerospace Force continued producing missiles and drones during recent fighting, using domestic expertise without importing foreign weapons or relying on "reverse engineering of weapons captured from the enemy."
Mohebbi also described Iran's growing self-sufficiency in weapons production as a "very big achievement."
Taleblu meanwhile emphasized the significance of the Caspian Sea basin, saying the world’s largest lake has "turned into a two-way sanctions-busting hub for both Iran and Russia."
"Iranian officials always claim self-sufficiency in their military industries," he said.
"But with domestic missile production significantly constrained due to the 40-Day War, the regime will be reliant on imports to build back, and especially at scale and at a faster rate.
"This is why efforts to constrain both land and sea trade in and out of Iran are a one-two punch for the regime."
The warnings come as Washington intensified pressure on Iran's regional trade routes , including its land crossings with Iraq , where Baghdad has reportedly resisted U.S. demands for full and broader border restrictions.
According to the Institute for the Study of War (ISW), Iraq has closed only one border crossing with Iran so far, despite reported American pressure to shut down most crossings between the two countries.
FRESH ACTIVITY EMERGES AT IRAN’S DEEPLY BURIED NUCLEAR SITE AS TRUMP WARNS IRAN NOT TO ‘GET CUTE’
Soldiers from the US-led coalition forces are seen during the handover of the K1 Air Base to the Iraqi Army from the US-led coalition in Kirkuk, Iraq on March 29, 2020. (Associated Press)
On Sunday, the U.S. Treasury pressed Iraq to close all border crossings with Iran except for two as part of Washington's policy of increasing economic pressure on Tehran, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said, according to Reuters .
The Iraqi government had closed the al-Shayeb crossing in southeastern Iraq on Oct. 21, to review security and install equipment to prevent smuggling of prohibited materials.
Iraqi political sources told Agence France-Presse that Washington had pressured Baghdad to close most Iran-Iraq border crossings to restrict trade and financial exchanges that could help Tehran withstand U.S. sanctions, ISW reported.
ISW also said that Iranian Ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh was pressuring tribal leaders in Iraq's Maysan province to push Iraqi officials and leaders of the Shiite Coordination Framework to reopen al-Shayeb.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Al-Sadegh is reportedly a member of the IRGC's Quds Force, which oversees the organization's foreign operations.
The institute assessed that Baghdad's limited response likely reflects efforts to balance its relationship with Washington against the influence of Iranian-backed political factions.
Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
articles.title_zh: Nvidia announces probe into CEO Huang amid reports China spied on him
articles.content_orig:
Jensen Huang "is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA," the company said.
Tech giant NVIDIA has announced an investigation of its CEO amid allegations that he was the subject of an intelligence-gathering effort by the Chinese.
"The NVIDIA Board is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort," the company said in a statement Sunday, adding that a "committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation."
Jensen "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the NVIDIA statement further said.
"While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," according to the statement.
"The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders," the statement further said.
"The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," according to the statement.
The New York Times reported late last month that Huang, who runs the world's largest computer chip manufacturer, was targeted by a Chinese espionage plot centered around a woman they identified as Alice Huang, a top executive at Singapore-based data company Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials determined was funneling information to Beijing and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang.
The Chinese government has denied the allegations, calling them "baseless and purely slanderous smears against China."
Neither Alice Huang nor her employer, Megaspeed International, responded to ABC News' request for comment after the New York Times story broke.
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected" and are part of Jensen Huang's job, an NVIDIA spokesperson told ABC News at the time.
However, NVIDIA on Sunday shared with ABC News an internal message Jensen Huang sent to employees, in which he said he was "unfaithful" to his wife.
"My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," the message said, in part. It did not name Alice Huang nor any other person.
Addressing NVIDIA staff, partners and shareholders, Huang went on to say "my responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence."
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," Huang's message said.
Following the New York Times report, congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China sent a letter to Jensen Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the letter said, in part. It is not known if Huang will appear before the committee.
“Today’s news will not slow NVIDIA. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption," an NVIDIA spokesperson told ABC News Sunday.

articles.title_orig: Newport Beach fishermen find Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water 20 miles off coast
articles.title_zh: Newport Beach fishermen find Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water 20 miles off coast
articles.content_orig:
Two Newport Beach fishermen found a Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast while returning home from a fishing trip near Catalina Island on Friday.
Sean Norton and Grant Garrett were fishing for marlin in the morning. By noon, they had rescued the 37-year-old man who had been treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast in the middle of the Pacific Ocean.
"I'm like, 'Yeah, it's a human being. Stop the boat; let's get all of our lines in," Garrett said, recalling the moment the boat's captain spotted the man in the water.
"Grant and I each got an arm and lifted him up," Norton said. "He was in total shock."
Garrett said when the man came to, he told them he was a pianist on the 14-deck Royal Caribbean cruise ship called the "Ovation of the Seas," which was en route to Ensenada, Mexico out of Long Beach.
"The only thing he said to me was, 'Thank you. I thought I was gonna die,'" Norton said.
After pulling him from the water, the crew put out an emergency maritime call, and a group of Newport Beach lifeguards responded to help.
"It was approximately 15 to 20 miles offshore, pretty much in the middle of the ocean," Battalion Chief Adam Yacenda said. They believe he may have gone overboard from the ship about nine hours before he was found, at around 2:30 a.m.
The man, who still hasn't been identified, was hospitalized after the ordeal and is expected to survive, according to the U.S. Coast Guard, which is investigating the incident and how he went overboard.
"You have this crazy super El Niño year. This guy was in the water for probably 10 hours, but the water's 76 degrees," Norton said. "A different year, no way he makes it."
In a statement to CBS LA, a Royal Caribbean Group spokesperson shared, "We are providing support and assistance to our crew member during this difficult time. To respect the privacy of our employee, we have no additional details to share."

articles.title_orig: Europeans will join Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French foreign minister says
articles.title_zh: Europeans will join Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French foreign minister says
articles.content_orig:
A view through the destroyed walls of a kindergarten shows a large bomb crater and a damaged residential apartment building following a missile attack in Kyiv, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption
European officials will turn up for the U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates this week, France's foreign minister said Sunday, days after the Kremlin had insisted there could be no role for European powers at the meeting.
"France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio. He did not say who would represent Paris, or whether French or other European officials would take part directly in negotiations, or simply observe.
The meetings, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, had previously been presented as a three-way session between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.
Talking to a Russian news channel on Friday, he accused European governments of failing to decide who speaks for them, while acknowledging that security talks would at some point require Europe's involvement.
On Thursday, President Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and said a coming agreement was "going to involve more than Ukraine," adding he could even say it "might involve all of Europe."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN on Friday that he had not been given details of the agreement Trump had referenced, and warned: "For me, it's not simple, and it can be dangerous." He invoked the 1945 Yalta conference, where Allied leaders settled Europe's division without the involvement of several affected countries.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attend a press conference in Berlin, Germany, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ebrahim Noroozi/AP hide caption
This will be the fourth round of talks between the two warring nations brokered by the Trump administration, and the first since those in Geneva this February. Earlier U.S.-brokered meetings have made little progress, and the chances of a breakthrough have been reduced as the Trump administration focused on its war with Iran.
Moscow confirmed it would return to the negotiating table only following a visit by U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in October. Those talks saw Putin announce the release of an American prisoner from a Russian jail — an apparent Kremlin gesture to President Trump's earlier lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Ukraine was vehemently opposed to the fuel sales — arguing they helped replenish Moscow's war chest.
Witkoff has said the agenda for these latest talks will include postwar security arrangements and de-escalation of the conflict and humanitarian issues, shortly after Melania Trump helped broker a limited ceasefire that allowed humanitarian aid to enter a town inside Russian-occupied Ukraine.
Russia's delegation will again be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline Putin aide who has participated in most talks with Ukraine since the unsuccessful first set of discussions all the way back in March 2022.
For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky, a deputy head of the General Staff's operations directorate, alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.
This more senior lineup could indicate that Moscow is readier than before to address thorny political and military questions. But the U.S. think tankInstitute for the Study of War suggested some of those same Russian officials have in fact previously sought to slow down previous talks or push harder on Moscow's demands.
The gaps between the two countries remain substantial. Russia has demanded that Ukraine give up large parts of its territory and renounce NATO membership. Zelenskyy has repeatedly insisted any security commitments should be clearly spelled out, including who would act, and how, if Russia attacked again.
Russian President Vladimir Putin, right, interacts with people at the monument to merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky, leaders of the struggle against foreign invaders in 1612, in Red Square in Moscow, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, during National Unity Day celebrations. Yuri Kochetkov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
Some analysts expect little. In an op-ed for the Atlantic Council think tank, the former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst argued that Putin had rejected every U.S. proposal Kyiv accepted and preferred participating in peace talks than pursuing actual peace. "Perhaps the only outcome of the talks," he wrote, "will be to agree to another round."
The meetings in the United Arab Emirates also follow Democrats' midterm victories, which Zelenskyy said could improve Ukraine's chances of more U.S. aid.
Russia, too, may be looking to push for the Trump administration's outlines of a Ukraine deal — before a Democratic-controlled Congress arrives come January.
Also hovering over the talks — the prospect of Trump, Xi, and Putin gathering for a trilateral meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China later this month. While details remain murky, all sides have confirmed discussions are underway.
And as officials travel to Abu Dhabi to talk peace, the war has raged on regardless.
Zelenskyy said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area overnight Saturday, with only four intercepted, accusing Moscow of treating diplomacy "as a form of aggression."
In southern Ukraine, the death toll from a guided-bomb strike Monday on an aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha rose to at least 55.

articles.title_orig: Elon Musk’s Austin home targeted by well-funded leftist groups aboard party buses
articles.title_zh: Elon Musk’s Austin home targeted by well-funded leftist groups aboard party buses
articles.content_orig:
Fox News host Greg Gutfeld and the ‘Gutfeld!’ panel discuss Hillary Clinton saying she wants to force Elon Musk to testify to Congress if President Donald Trump pardons him.
Three far-left nonprofits with combined annual revenues of $56.1 million escalated their protests against SpaceX and Tesla CEO Elon Musk this week by targeting his Austin-area home with a seemingly innocuous post-election "party" featuring two chartered buses, music, speeches, theatrical Cybertruck piñatas and dancing to Queen’s "We Will Rock You."
The event’s organizers – VOCAL-TX, the fiscally-sponsored project of a New York 501(c)(3) nonprofit; the Center for Popular Democracy Inc., a 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Brooklyn; and People’s Action, a 501(c)(4) political nonprofit based in Chicago – framed the Saturday event as a tame "People Over Billionaires Election After Party."
The demonstration reflected growing coordination among leftist networks worldwide, from Paris to Portland, Ore., supplying organizers, transportation, coalition partners, event platforms, messaging and other logistical support for actions presented as "grassroots." As Democratic politicians threaten investigations into Trump’s corporate backers, including Musk, the street protests help create the appearance of bottom-up support.
The leaders of the organizations behind the "After Party," held in West Lake Hills, Tex., where Musk owns a sprawling home, didn’t provide comment in response to queries from Fox News Digital, but they have insisted in the past that their local protests are the result of "organic" organizing in communities.
A now-ubiquitous, mass-produced anti-Musk "I AM STEALING FROM YOU" poster, featuring the tech billionaire with creepy eyes, has appeared at demonstrations nationwide and was also on display at the Austin protest outside his home.
At a May Day protest in Washington, D.C., on May 1, 2025, blocks from the White House, a protester from the communist Party for Socialism and Liberation carries a mass-produced poster created by a Democratic nonprofit to vilify Tesla CEO Elon Musk. (Asra Q. Nomani)
WHO’S FUNDING AMERICA’S PROTEST UNREST? FOX NATION'S NEW 'RIOT INC.' FOLLOWS THE MONEY TO FIND OUT
This weekend’s organizers helped lead the " Tesla Takedown" protests that sometimes turned ugly last year. According to a Fox News Digital investigation, 258 organizations with combined annual revenues of an estimated $2.6 billion were behind those protests.
At Saturday’s event, participants arrived at the property in two blue Fly-Rides party buses and additional vehicles. Organizers blasted music including Queen’s "We Will Rock You," over loudspeakers.
"We'll bring the music, you bring the dance moves! This is family friendly, peaceful and FUN event!" the organizers wrote, promoting the event.
The Austin American-Statesman covered the event and cast it playfully, with the headline "Dozens party outside Elon Musk's West Lake Hills home after campaign donations fell flat." It wrote about how organizers led a "Love Train" conga line and distributed party hats and refreshments, including cider.
The organizations behind the campaign are veterans of the professional protest industry. While this event was peaceful, the rhetoric of demonization and polarization at protests causes researchers at organizations like the Network Contagion Research Institute to conclude that that they can create a "permission structure" for political violence.
Last week, Musk blamed the issue on the U.S. military. (Getty Images)
‘ASTROTURF’: CRITICS SPECULATE TESLA PROTESTS ARE NOT A GRASSROOTS MOVEMENT, BUT A CAREFULLY ORGANIZED CAMPAIGN
The three nonprofits behind this weekend’s protests are part of a powerful national tax-exempt nonprofit industry that has increasingly taken to the streets over the past decade in coordinated, orchestrated campaigns in local communities, creating the image of homegrown organic demonstrations.
The three groups reported $56.1 million in combined 2024 revenue, according to their most recent tax filings.
Organizers promoted the event as a peaceful celebration of voters rejecting the influence of wealthy donors. About 60 people attended, according to estimates.
The demonstration followed in the spirit of the very coordinated "Tesla Takedown" protests launched at Texas dealerships in early 2025, when activists organized demonstrations against Tesla and Musk over his political activities and role in the new Trump administration and the Department of Government Efficiency , called DOGE. Those protests led to vandalism against Tesla vehicles and dealerships. A wider network of openly pro-communist groups, including Freedom Road Socialist Organization, carried posters with messages like "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES. WE NEED SOCIALISM."
Congressional lawmakers and Justice Department prosecutors are investigating an American-born, Shanghai-based tycoon, Neville Roy Singham, for funding and backing pro-communist groups. Some of those groups, including the Party for Socialism and Liberation, ANSWER Coalition, CodePink and People's Forum, have supported the regular protests that have hit America's streets, including the anti-Musk demonstrations.
On May 1, 2025, members of the Freedom Road Socialist Organization protested in Washington, D.C., blocks from the White House to support labor rights. "DOWN WITH BILLIONAIRES," a sign read, with an image of Elon Musk. "WE NEED SOCIALISM." (Asra Q. Nomani)
DEMOCRATS SET SIGHTS ON ELON MUSK PROBE AFTER MIDTERM WINS, BUT PRITZKER DRAWS A SURPRISING LINE
Much like the networks behind "No Kings," "Hands Off," "ICE Out" and other protests over the past year, the financial filings of the organizations behind this weekend’s demonstration show the scale of the infrastructure behind these groups.
The Center for Popular Democracy reported $40.9 million in 2024 revenue. People’s Action Institute reported $2.1 million, and Voices of Community Activists and Leaders Inc., or VOCAL-NY, which fiscally sponsors VOCAL-TX, reported $13.1 million. The organizations are separate entities, and the figures don’t represent a shared operating budget.
VOCAL-TX’s donation page identifies VOCAL-NY as its 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor and sister organization. VOCAL-NY describes the organization as a statewide grassroots membership group focused on "building the power of low-income people" impacted by "HIV/AIDS, drug policy, mass incarceration, the war on drugs and homelessness." It says its work is "accomplished through community organizing, campaigns & harm reduction services."
The Center for Popular Democracy Inc. lists VOCAL-TX among its affiliates and describes itself as a network of "grassroots" organizations operating across dozens of states, building a "representative, multiracial society and government where all thrive, no exceptions," according to its nonprofit mission statement.
The protesters’ goal, according to the organization's website, is to send a crystal clear message that they are against Tesla CEO Elon Musk, describing itself as a decentralized grassroots movement that will "protest Tesla for as long as Elon Musk continues to shred public services." Organizers plan to hold rallies at over 200 Tesla location across the U.S. (Getty Images)

articles.title_orig: Train crash kills seven, injures dozens near Egypt’s Cairo city
articles.title_zh: Train crash kills seven, injures dozens near Egypt’s Cairo city
articles.content_orig:
At least seven people have been killed and more than 125 others injured in a train crash on the outskirts of Cairo in Egypt’s Giza province, according to the country’s Health Ministry.
A train travelling between Giza and Fayoum on Sunday ran into the back of another train on the Cairo-to-Aswan route, causing the latter to derail from its tracks onto a countryside road in the district of al-Ayyat, authorities said.
Emergency rescue teams and cranes were dispatched to the scene to clear the wreckage and restore train services to their normal schedule as soon as possible, Egyptian National Railways said.
Authorities say more than 70 ambulances were involved in transport and evacuation operations at the scene of the crash, with casualties taken to nearby hospitals.
President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said he was following the accident “with great concern”, and had directed authorities to conduct an urgent investigation to “hold accountable anyone found to have been negligent”.
Witnesses described chaotic rescue efforts after the collision, as villagers, first responders and railway workers scrambled to reach passengers trapped inside overturned carriages.
Abdel Wahed Mohamed, 31, who was sitting at a nearby cafe when the collision occurred, said the Aswan-bound train had stopped, when the Fayoum-bound train crashed into it.
“The train overturned at around 1:30 pm [11:30 GMT]. Six carriages overturned,” he said, adding that victims suffered a range of injuries, including head wounds and broken limbs.
Another witness, Ahmed Moussa, 25, said rescuers dug beneath one overturned carriage to reach trapped passengers.
“There were people piled on top of each other inside,” he said, adding that he saw two women among the dead.
Taha Abdel Tawab, 43, said he “saw a young man leaving the train carrying his dead father”.
Al-Ayyat district, where the collision happened, is also the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster .
In 2002, more than 370 people were killed when a fire swept through a train carrying holiday travellers south of Cairo. In 2009, multiple train crashes in the area killed dozens.
Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the cross-country network – one of the largest in Africa – is in need of modernisation.
Over the past decade, Egypt has poured billions of dollars into updating its transport infrastructure, including new highways and high-speed rail lines, but has yet to overhaul much of its dated train services .

articles.title_zh: What does the Jensen Huang case mean for Nvidia's chip sales to China? No rules have changed so far
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted to having an affair with a woman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly suspects is a Chinese spy.
Huang, who heads a leading AI chipmaker and is an ally of President Donald Trump , apologized in a message to the company, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife,” according to The New York Times .
“My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Nvidia announced in a press release Sunday that its board was opening an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.”
Late last month, the Times reported that Huang had formed a close relationship with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, a Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data center.
Alice Huang is considered by U.S. officials to be a Chinese spy, feeding information to Beijing, according to the report, which cited sources briefed on the surveillance of Alice Huang and other officials and industry experts.
“The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” Sunday’s company press release read.
“While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information.”
CEO Huang supports the investigation and has agreed to cooperate with it, the board said.
There was no word of Huang’s position being in jeopardy, with the board saying it “has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.”
Nvidia is one of the hottest companies in the stock market right now, given the popularity of its chips. It has a market capitalization of roughly 4.5 trillion and was trading at nearly $240 per share early last month.
Huang, like other tech leaders, has flocked to Trump as the president embraces AI. The Nvidia leader and his wife, Lori Huang, attended a state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House in September. His attendance wasn’t unusual, given that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg were also there.

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot tapped to form Israeli government
articles.content_orig:
Nov. 8 (UPI) -- Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot said he is open to including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the coalition he is working to build.
Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming the country's next government by President Isaac Herzog, also suggested far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich would be welcomed to join.
"If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented," Eisenkot said.
Eisenkot, who has six weeks to form a new government , said he would represent all segments of Israeli society.
Meanwhile, Herzog said Israel faces uncertainties after the U.S. midterm elections last week, which saw several candidates critical of Israel and military support by Washington win seats in the U.S. Senate and House.
"The State of Israel needs a stable government," Herzog said, citing a "new political reality" in the U.S.
Eisenkot was the head of the Israeli military from 2015 to 2019 and served as an observer in Netanyahu's war cabinet for the first eight months of the country's war on Gaza after the Hamas attacks on Israel in October 2023.
Still, Arab-led parties have endorsed Eisenkot to replace Netanyahu.
In Israel's election last month, Eisenkot's alliance of four parties won 48 seats in parliament, while Netanyah's right-wing and religious bloc took 53 seats. Each missed the 61 seats needed for a majority. Arab-led parties won 19 seats, a record.
Eisenkot has rejected forming a government with the Arab-led parties, even though it would give him a bloc of 67 seats. He would secure 61 seats by winning over two ultra-religious parties, United Torah Judaism and Shas.
Eisenkot may be able to form a government with less than 61 votes by winning a confidence vote in parliament.

articles.title_zh: Sequoia partners reportedly blindsided when Roelof Botha joined SpaceX board
articles.content_orig:
Buy One Founder Summit Ticket, Get a Second for Free. Register now.
Founder Summit begins Nov. 4, 9:00 a.m. ET. Get your pass savings & deals before it starts. REGISTER HERE.
Sequoia Capital announced some major changes this week, including the closure of its London office, the merger of its early-stage and growth teams, and the end of its Scouts program .
Now, the Financial Times has published a report painting all of this as an attempt to undo the legacy of former leader Roelof Botha, who stepped down as the firm’s steward last year . An unnamed source told the FT that Botha “loved process and hierarchy,” while “the rest of the team didn’t.”
Apparently, not everyone is on-board with the changes, with another source firing back that this seems like an “erasure of Sequoia’s heritage, not Roelof’s legacy.”
The break between Botha and his old firm reportedly deepened after Botha joined the SpaceX board this summer. (Botha and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk previously worked together at PayPal.) A source told the FT that Sequoia’s partners were blindsided by the announcement, because Botha “didn’t ask compliance, he didn’t get sign off from the partnership” — even though his new role could complicate the firm’s ability to trade its $20 billion stake.
A Sequoia spokesperson said that the firm continues to “collaborate closely” with Botha.

articles.title_orig: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.title_zh: UN agency for Palestinian refugees eyeing major restructuring
articles.content_orig:
The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) is considering a major restructuring that could see thousands of its employees laid off and some of its responsibilities transferred to other bodies, including US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace, according to multiple media reports citing diplomatic sources.
The reported proposal is spearheaded by UNRWA’s acting commissioner-general, Christian Saunders, and comes as the agency faces a severe financial crisis.
Trump’s Board of Peace (BoP), established under the framework endorsed by the UN Security Council in November 2025, is tasked with overseeing Gaza’s transitional governance, reconstruction, economic recovery, and coordination of humanitarian assistance.
The BoP has been explicit in its opposition to the UN agency set up for Palestinian refugees only, making it clear in a July 1 statement that “UNRWA has no place in the new Gaza .”
“We are turning the page on the complex of perpetual aid dependency and conflict. The people of Gaza deserve better,” the BoP said in a social media post on September 25.
In the same post, the BoP said it would “only work with trusted partners who will deliver for the people of Gaza and contribute to a de-radicalized Strip. UNRWA fails on those litmus tests.”
However, the Associated Press reported, also on September 25, that BoP representatives have held several private meetings with UNRWA officials. A BoP official acknowledged that some of the agency’s programs and vetted employees could continue if they were effective and accountable, while maintaining that the UN body’s institutional role was ending.
UN Watch’s Hillel Neuer posted last week that there is a plan to unravel UNRWA, which has long faced criticism from Israel, the United States, and UN Watch over allegations of links between some of its employees and terrorist organizations such as Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) – including participating in October 7 and holding hostages.
According to Israel Hayom , which cited Arab and Western diplomatic sources, discussions have taken place about transferring some of UNRWA’s responsibilities to the BoP and other bodies.
Some of the agency’s remit could reportedly also be transferred to the Palestinian Authority (PA) in the West Bank.
The reported proposal was presented by Saunders at a meeting of UNRWA’s Advisory Commission, with the agency’s financial difficulties cited as a central reason for the restructuring. Saunders told Anadolu Agency on October 20 that the agency’s deficit stood at approximately $70 million.
“If we don’t receive money in the very near future, I will have to take some regrettable actions in order to ensure that we’re able to finish the year and to pay our staff salaries,” Saunders warned.
The head of the Arab Staff Union in Gaza, Mustafa Al-Ghoul, told the Mondoweiss anti-Zionist news site last week that UNRWA had dismissed around 1,000 staff in Gaza and let 2,000 retire without replacing them, leaving roughly 10,500.
Saunders gave the same figures in the Anadolu Agency interview, saying “We have 10,500 personnel on the ground [in the Gaza Strip].”
He also expressed support for the broader international framework for Gaza, saying: “ US President Trump ’s 20-point plan, UN Security Council Resolution 2803, the Board of Peace, and the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza – we are completely behind these efforts.”
Separately, Swiss French-language daily newspaper Le Temps published an investigation last week saying that Saunders plans for UNRWA to close its doors “within four or five years.” This has not yet been independently verified.
Under the UN-backed framework, the BoP is to exercise transitional authority in Gaza until the PA has completed its reform program and can securely and effectively resume control. In the meantime, the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza is intended to serve as an interim technocratic administration.
Currently, UNRWA purports to be assisting more than 1.7 million Palestinians in Gaza, providing healthcare through 11 centers, schooling for approximately 300,000 children, and drinking water for around 820,000 people.
It also says it provides essential services to nearly six million Palestinian refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, and the West Bank.

articles.title_orig: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.title_zh: China's half-price Rolls-Royce: Yangwang Altior is a lavish alternative to a Phantom limo
articles.content_orig:
By ROB HULL, MOTORING EDITOR
Updated: 13:34 EDT, 8 November 2026
We've had the Temu Range Rover; now there's an AliExpress Roller.
Chinese brand Yangwang, a spin-off from electric car giant BYD, has unveiled a new battery-powered luxury vehicle called the Altior, and it bears a striking resemblance to the iconic British Rolls-Royce Phantom limousine – but for around half the price.
At 5.6m long, with a vast bonnet and grille, rear-hinged coach doors, a palatial interior and umbrellas stowed inside the door panels, there's no hiding which ostentatious motor it has firmly set its sights on.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, with the car 'expressing an ambition to elevate the experience of luxury through cultural depth, personal expression and technological progress', Yangwang says.
Just 399 are going to be produced and reports in China suggest pre-orders are available from 2million yuan, which equates to around £230,000.
That puts it closer to the £250,000 Rolls-Royce Ghost than the flagship £450,000 Phantom, though that's before taking into account heavily subsidised pricing in China's domestic market.
Its global premiere in Abu Dhabi this weekend comes just days after car registration figures revealed that Jaecoo's 'Temu Range Rover' 7 SUV was the UK's best-selling new model for a second successive month .
The runaway success of the Range Rover Velar lookalike is the clearest sign yet that Chinese brands are coming for the old guard of established luxury carmakers. And with the Altior, it appears not even Rolls-Royce is safe.
This is the new Yangwang Altior limousine - a luxury Rolls-Royce Phantom rival from Chinese EV giant, BYD
While the Rolls-Royce Phantom and Ghost feature a gutsy 6.75-litre twin-turbocharged V12 petrol engine, the Yangwang Altior is a far greener proposition.
It uses a version of the quad-electric motor setup deployed in the Chinese firm's other models, the U8 SUV and U9 supercar. That's likely to produce more than 1,000bhp and will allow it to perform a tank turn , rotating each wheel independently to spin the vehicle on its own axis.
Providing the energy for the e-motors is BYD's second-generation Blade Battery technology.
As such, it's claimed to be capable of travelling more than 621 miles on a full charge. However, this is based on Chinese efficiency tests that are historically a shade more optimistic than Europe's cycle, which would be closer to 520 miles.
The battery is compatible with BYD's network of Flash Charging stations, of which there are 10,000 already in China and a promise to install 300 here in the UK .
The ground-breaking devices can deliver up to 1,500kW of power and top up a battery pack from 10 to 70 per cent charge in as little as five minutes, before reaching full charge in less than ten.
That's not all in terms of technological advances.
The Yangwang boasts a suite of chassis tech that means it can float if there are flash floods or the driver 'accidentally enters water'. And it can continue tracking in a straight line when one of the tyres suffers a high-speed blowout on the motorway.
The Altior also taps into BYD's God's Eye A assisted-driving system, which includes parking-space-to-parking-space navigation assistance. This enables the car to drive itself from one car park to another, even when they are hundreds of miles apart.
The suspension is clever too. The brand's DiSus active body control system uses cameras to read the road ahead and adjusts damping in real time, meaning occupants won't feel potholes or changes in road surfaces while stretched out in the back.
Altior means 'higher' in Latin, as BYD's spin-off Yangwang looks to enter a more opulent market with its latest model. And it certain strikes a resemblance to the Rolls-Royce Phantom
Squint slightly and there's no mistaking the Rolls-Royce-inspired silhouette.
The elongated bonnet, despite there being no 12-cylinder combustion engine lurking beneath it, and the glitzy upright grille are trademarks of the 122-year-old British marque.
The Altior's front end is described as a 'masterpiece of high jewellery'.
'Meticulous selection, polishing and individual placement create a composition that responds to changing light, revealing new depth and brilliance as the viewpoint moves,' the Chinese manufacturer says.
Its lights are a little special too, featuring 12 individual elements that rotate from the outside to the centre to create a 'ceremonial welcome' when the owner approaches.
At 5.6m long, the Altior (pictured left) is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom (pictured right)
Like all Roller limousines, the Chinese Yangwang has rear-hinged coach doors
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom
Is it time for European luxury car makers to fear China’s fast-rising electric rivals?
At 5.6m long, the Altior is 5.5cm longer than the Ghost and 16cm shorter than the Phantom.
However, the Yangwang's other dimensions, including a width of 2m, a height of almost 1.6m and a wheelbase of 3.5m, are almost like-for-like with the bigger of the two Rolls-Royces.
Twenty-one-inch wheels are standard, with the dish-style monoblock design bearing more than a passing resemblance to the disc rims available on a Phantom.
The doors also open in the fashion for which Rolls-Royce is famed, providing generous access to the opulent interior.
The finely crafted bespoke umbrellas hidden in each door panel, much like those in a Rolls-Royce, are said to be inspired by the circular wooden roof of the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at China's Temple of Heaven complex.
The cockpit is the least Roller-like part of the car. While the British luxury firm attempts to conceal tech for a traditional look, the Yangwang has a dashboard-wide high-definition screen
Exactly like Rolls-Royces, though, the Chinese limo has bespoke, hand-crafted umbrellas hidden in a compartment within the doors
Step inside and the cabin – dubbed a 'private lounge' – is awash with only the highest-quality materials.
These include hammer-tested metal switches, pure-wool floor mats, real-wood veneers, 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons and semi-aniline leather upholstery.
The designers have even mounted polished yellow jade gemstones inside the vertical air vents, while the silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs.
The cockpit itself looks a little less Rolls-Royce-esque, even if it does feature a chrome-rimmed steering wheel wrapped in beautifully finished leather.
While the British car maker generally tries to subtly conceal much of its modern technology up front, the Yangwang has a dashboard-spanning digital glass display. This incorporates an instrument cluster with classic-style digital dials and an enormous infotainment screen featuring a laptop-style taskbar of icons.
But it's the rear compartment that well-heeled customers will want to know about.
The cabin is as palatial as you'd expect from a Rolls-Royce or Bentley limo. It boasts aviation-style zero-gravity seats, real-wood veneers and 48 jewellery-inspired control buttons
There's a fridge in the rear and in the front, two champagne flute holders and a control panel that means you won't have to converse with your chauffeur at all
There's plenty of artistry too. Silk-embroidered door panels feature cloud and thunder-pattern motifs
The four-seat layout is almost perfectly symmetrical and 'gives each occupant a clearly defined personal space' where the owner in the back can feel entirely separate from Jeeves behind the wheel by elevating a divider between them.
Owners won't need to ask their chauffeur for anything, either.
Rear occupants can access all key functions through the central console, including lowering the front passenger seat at the touch of a button to provide an uninterrupted view ahead.

articles.title_orig: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.title_zh: King leads solemn Remembrance Sunday service at Cenotaph
articles.content_orig:
King Charles III led the nation in a solemn two-minute silence on Remembrance Sunday in London to honour veterans who had died in conflict.
On a stone-grey autumn morning, he laid a wreath at the Cenotaph in Whitehall before a march-past by 10,000 armed forces veterans.
That included a shrinking number of World War Two veterans, with 12 taking part this year, including 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who described it as a "very emotional day".
Meanwhile, the number of former prime ministers reached a record high, with nine lined up to lay wreaths, while Andy Burnham attended for the first time as the current occupant of No 10 Downing Street.
And for the first time, the leader of Reform UK, Nigel Farage, had enough MPs in Parliament to qualify to lay a wreath alongside other major party leaders.
The Prince of Wales and the Princess Royal were among royals in attendance, along with military chiefs, senior politicians, diplomats and faith leaders, watched by big crowds squeezed behind railings along Whitehall.
Queen Camilla and the Princess of Wales watched from a balcony above the Cenotaph in the Foreign Office.
Among the flags on the roof of that Whitehall building was the Ukrainian blue and yellow. It went up when Russia invaded and four years later it is now visibly frayed - a reminder of the length of that war and of current threats.
At 11:00 GMT, as the first strike of Big Ben echoed from the nearby Houses of Parliament, the big two-minute silence filled the usually frenetic streets, before the playing of the Last Post.
The King had his eyes closed, the crowds in Whitehall stopped for their own thoughts, in a rare moment of calm in the capital.
The poignant parade past the Cenotaph included representatives of about 340 different military and civilian groups, from the Royal Naval Association and the Royal Marines Association to Transport for London and the Royal National Lifeboat Institute.
Alongside those marching were flotillas of disability scooters and families helping veterans in wheelchairs.
Those who took part in WW2 are now increasingly frail - and there were 12 participants in the march-past compared to 20 last year. The oldest participant this year was aged 105.
Taking part for the first time was 103-year-old Annie Duplock, who had been part of the Land Army that had helped to feed the country at war.
She had joined the Land Army in 1940 as a 16-year-old, having lied about her age, and worked on a farm in Leicestershire.
"I feel very honoured to be taking part in the parade and to represent the Land Girls. I'm very excited, although a little apprehensive as I don't quite know what to expect," she said.
"I think it will be a very emotional day, bringing back memories of all those who didn't return home. It will be lovely to be there and remember them."
Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the annual event was a time to "reflect on the selflessness and courage it takes to commit your life to protecting others".
He earlier announced that he wanted to tackle the problem of homelessness among ex-service personnel to "ensure that any veteran sleeping rough is offered appropriate accommodation before Christmas".
Mark Atkinson, the director general of the Royal British Legion, said: "As we come together on Remembrance Sunday, we pay tribute to all those who have served and sacrificed, from generations past to those still serving today."
Remembrance events took place across the country as thousands gathered to pay their respects to those who died in past conflicts.
First Minister of Scotland John Swinney placed a wreath at the Stone of Remembrance outside the City Chambers during an event in Edinburgh.
Veterans, military personnel and cadets also marched through the centres of British cities such as Manchester, Birmingham and Leeds.
A silent poppy drop was held as part of the Festival of Remembrance at Durham Cathedral while wreaths were laid at Canterbury Cathedral.
Separately, the Duke of Sussex was seen attending a Remembrance service in the market town of Brackley in Northamptonshire.
For more than a century, the national Remembrance event has been held around the Cenotaph.
The monument was built as a focal point for honouring those who had fought and died in World War One, including those who had no grave, and as a place to mourn for those families who might not be able to visit war cemeteries overseas.
The word "cenotaph" means "empty tomb" in Greek and it was designed by the architect Sir Edwin Lutyens in a simple, austere style, with no sense of triumphalism and with almost no decoration.
The monument had been originally built in 1919 as a temporary, plaster and wood structure. But it proved so popular with the public that it was replaced in 1920 with a permanent version, in the same design but in stone.
It was opened at 11:00 on 11 November 1920 by King George V. His great-grandson, Charles, was there again, on an overcast morning 106 years later, to continue paying respect.

articles.title_orig: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.title_zh: Chinese carmaker BYD’s offices in Netherlands raided over JLR ‘copycat car’ claim
articles.content_orig:
Bailiffs reportedly seized digital records before court case over alleged intellectual property breaches on Land Rover Defender
Bailiffs acting for Jaguar Land Rover raided the Dutch offices of a Chinese “copycat” rival before a legal showdown this week over whether its “Defender clone” infringes intellectual property rights.
Bailiffs acting on behalf of JLR reportedly seized digital records from the offices of Chinese carmaker BYD in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August, according to the Sunday Times.
The raid took place before a court case in the The Hague this week which will decide whether the BYD has a case to answer over allegations that its Ti7 SUV infringes the intellectual property of the Land Rover Defender.
Motoring experts have likened BYD’s seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV to the Defender since it went on sale in China in September last year. The company is scheduled to launch the vehicle, which the BBC’s Top Gear magazine called the “Chinese Defender clone” , in the UK market in January at a price of £47,995, undercutting the Defender by more than £20,000.
BYD says on its website that “an unapologetically boxy profile delivers the imposing, chunky design that finds favour among SUV buyers, yet delivers a contemporary look”.
The price of JLR’s seven-seat Defender 110 starts from £68,465and is one of the country’s bestselling cars. The UK-based carmaker, which is owned by India’s Tata Motors, sold 29,500 Defenders to retail customers between July and September this year, compared with 25,370a year earlier.
The raid in the Netherlands was carried out by court-ordered bailiffs, with JLR suspecting that BYD reverse-engineered some of the technology that could be used in the Ti7, the Times reported. JLR wanted to secure the digital records before they could be destroyed.
JLR and BYD declined to comment on the “ongoing legal proceedings”.
The dispute with BYD is not the first legal case JLR has pursed against a Chinese company over copycat allegations. It won a legal case to stop Jiangling Motor Corporation selling a copycat vehicle in 2019 after a three-year court battle.
after newsletter promotion
In some cases JLR has taken a collaborative approach to dealing with the rise of China’s carmakers. It agreed to form a joint venture with Chery in a 2012 deal which later included licensing its discontinued Freelander brand with the company.
Chery’s Jaecoo model, which is not part of the joint venture, has been called the Temu Range Rover because of its similarities to the JLR vehicle after years of collaboration between the pair. It costs £10,000 less than JLR’s Range Rover.
The Jaecoo was the bestselling car in the UK in October, with 10,813 registrations, taking its market share from 2.07% to 4.30%, according to the Society of Motor Manufacturers & Traders. JLR’s sales of the Range Rover fell to 43,300 in the third quarter of this year, from 47,196 cars sold in the same months last year.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang reportedly targeted by Beijing-recruited spy
articles.content_orig:
Lawmakers from both sides of the aisle are ramping up calls for investigations into reports of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy. Some are also questioning what the Trump administration knew about the matter.
"The more I learn about the insane relationship between the Trump Administration, Chinese spies, and AI billionaires, the more I'm convinced there is nothing this administration does that isn't corrupt," Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del., posted on X on Saturday. "Congress will investigate and get answers."
Coons is in line to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee when his party takes control of the chamber in January.
Three House Republican committee chairs sent a letter to Huang on Wednesday requesting that he sit for a closed-door briefing with lawmakers on Nov. 18, a day after the company is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People's Republic of China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the GOP lawmakers wrote in a letter to Huang .
The reports refer to Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based tech company that the U.S. has suspected of helping China circumvent artificial intelligence chip sales prohibitions.
Policymakers in the Trump administration received a memo last spring with intelligence identifying Alice Huang as having been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security and revealing her relationship with Nvidia's chief executive, The New York Times first reported on Friday.
When asked by the Times whether Huang would appear before lawmakers to discuss the matter, Nvidia spokesman John Rizzo declined to comment. "Our chief executive has an outstanding security team that accompanies him where needed," Mr. Rizzo said in a statement to the Times.
Rizzo said the Nvidia CEO's interactions with Ms. Huang were consistent with meetings he has had with any of Nvidia's customers, the Times reported .
Separately, Texas Republican Sen. John Cornyn shared a Times article published Saturday reporting that the Trump administration approved a Chinese firm, New Matrix, to assemble chips for Nvidia in Beijing. The Times found little evidence of meaningful operations at its listed address, despite Trump's Commerce Department clearing it for national security risks.
Cornyn called the report "outrageous" in his post on X .
Rep. Seth Magaziner, D-R.I., who sits on the House Committee on Homeland Security, called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify before Congress along with Huang.
Neither Nvidia nor the Commerce Department immediately responded to CNBC's request for comment.

Le Soleil newspaper said that most of the victims were from the Leona and Thieppe districts in the same department.
